correctness.rationale: In the complete-graph continuous-time rate model n_beta(n_alpha/(N-1))^q, super/subadditivity of positive power sums gives ordered focal set death rates and ordered entrance rates for any nested A-site sets, yielding a nonexplosive common-part sitewise coupling for q>1 and reverse for 0<q<1; q=1 coincides. The two-type focal count birth-death rates have mu_a/lambda_a=(a/(N-a))^(1-q), telescoping products equal binom(N-1,r)^(q-1), so the displayed H is the exact binary absorption probability. Applying the full multistate generator to H(a) leaves the exact signed competitor power-sum defect; finite absorption and Dynkin formula give the time integral. With at least two competitor opinions and interior a initially, the strictly signed positive first holding interval makes inequality strict. Independently solved a 15-state exact rational 4-person, three-opinion q=2 generator; all compared H-bounds/strictness and defect matched.
residual_risks: Only homogeneous complete graph, prescribed CTMC rates, positive q; no consensus-time ordering or arbitrary spatial network theorem. Finite-state calculation supports, does not establish arbitrary N.

value.rationale: An exact sharp all-time stochastic envelope and a signed exact finite-expected-time correction make the multistate process tractable without falsely pretending the focal count is Markov. Strictness identifies when additional competing opinions genuinely change fixation—a natural question for generalized voter dynamics.
